summary: The southern parcel of the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard along 22nd Street, drawn as one flexibly zoned parcel 'HDY1/2' in the D4D height figure (65 ft) and shown as commercial in the D4D Mid-Point scenario; like HDY3 it is outside Brookfield's 28-Acre Project and depends on the City exercising its option to buy the yard from PG&E. No sale, developer or construction has been recorded.

milestones.text: Mayor Lee and Supervisor Cohen introduce resolutions of intention to form Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard) to finance affordable housing within Pier 70 and Parcel K South
Capital Planning Committee briefed on the resolutions of intent to form the Hoedown Yard IRFD and issue bonds
Port Commission consents to zoning the Hoedown Yard (Assessor's Blocks 4120/002 and 4711/008A per the memo) into the Pier 70 Special Use District (Resolution 17-45) and recommends the IRFD (17-49)

Board of Supervisors adopts Resolution No. 234-18 (File 170880), the resolution of intention to establish Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard, Pier 70), calling its formation hearing for September 11, 2018; the resolution as introduced on July 25, 2017 had named October 24, 2017, a date the amendments of November 9 and December 5, 2017 and July 12, 2018 replaced before adoption, so the adopted resolution did not call a hearing for that date

Board of Supervisors passes the ordinance creating the district on first reading (its September 11, 2018 consideration had been continued), and the district's three qualified landowners cast all three votes in favor on each of four ballot measures, including formation, the financing plan and bonds of up to $91.9 million (2017 dollars)

Mayor approves Ordinance No. 248-18 (File 180772), creating Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard, Pier 70); the Board of Supervisors had finally passed it on October 23, 2018

Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) says the Hoedown Yard IRFD tax increment, one of three gap-funding sources for the affordable sites, is 'currently unavailable as market-rate development has yet to occur'

Port Commission Resolution 17-45 consents to zoning amendments establishing the Pier 70 Special Use District over the 28-Acre Site, the 20th & Illinois Street Parcel and the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard, and approves the Design for Development, bringing the Hoedown Yard into the SUD land-use and height framework as a future development parcel; the Hoedown Yard is not part of FC Pier 70's 28-Acre Project DDA

details.text: Use of HDY1/2: the D4D shows it as commercial in the Mid-Point and Maximum Office scenarios and residential in the Maximum Residential scenario; Retail and Service frontage for HDY3 and HDY1/2 may be combined on 22nd Street.
Disposition of the Hoedown Yard: under the 2017 DDA major terms, the City may ask the Hoedown Yard developer to build Irish Hill Park, paid with special taxes and the Port's share of tax increment.

Hoedown Yard financing district: it was created by Board of Supervisors Ordinance No. 248-18 (File 180772, approved November 2, 2018); unlike the Port IFD, its tax increment is meant to fund affordable housing, and the Port's August 2026 report calls these funding sources 'currently unavailable as market-rate development has yet to occur'.
Hoedown Yard name: the D4D describes the yard as currently owned by PG&E, with a City option to acquire it if PG&E can find a new location for its heavy industrial use.

open_questions: Whether the City has exercised its option to buy the Hoedown Yard from PG&E: no source read says. The Port's August 2026 Item 11A (p.2) still describes the yard as 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E'. The financing district itself was formed in 2018 (see the milestones).

The Port's 2026 proposed phasing plan (Item 11A, Exhibit A, p.8) shows the Hoedown Yard parcels (HDY1/2 and HDY3) outside every phase outline, since they are not part of the 28-Acre Project, so no phase is recorded here. Parcel K South, by contrast, sits inside the Phase 2B outline.
Assessor block/lot for the yard is given as 4120/002 and 4711/008A in the 2017 memo but 4120/002 and 4110/008A in the D4D; one is a typo, unresolved.

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: the Port's Aug 3, 2017 staff report (Item 11A, p.21, DDA major terms) says 'Parcel K North and the Hoedown Yard, while in the SUD, are not part of the Project', so the Hoedown Yard is a separate transaction from the 28-Acre Project; the Port's 2026 proposed phasing plan shows it outside every phase outline; no source read gives a schedule for the City's PG&E purchase option, so this record stays undated rather than borrow the 28-Acre Project's buildout target.
Size of the Hoedown Yard: the D4D gives approximately 3.6 acres and the DDA terms 'approximately 3-acre', in both cases including a 0.2-acre unbuilt Michigan Street right-of-way easement.
